Why CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer Is Trending

The Backend landscape is constantly evolving, and CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer has emerged as one of the fastest-growing projects this week. Several factors contribute to its momentum:

  1. Growing community: With 40 new stars this week alone, developer adoption is accelerating rapidly.
  2. Active maintenance: The project sees regular updates, ensuring compatibility with the latest ecosystem changes.
  3. Practical utility: A Proof of Concept demonstrating CET-compliant callstack spoofing in Rust. It leverages Windows Thread Pool and Enum Callback trampolining (e.g., EnumSystemLocalesEx) to forge a pristine, hardware-aligned call stack for indirect syscall evasion.

If you're working in Backend, this is definitely a project worth watching — and adopting.

Quick Start

Get started with CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer in minutes:

# Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/MrTiz/CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer # Navigate to project cd CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer # Check the README for detailed setup instructions

For full documentation and advanced usage, visit the official GitHub repository.

Final Thoughts

CET-Enum-CallStack-Spoofer is a solid addition to any developer's toolkit. With its growing community, active development, and practical design, it's well worth your time to evaluate. Star it on GitHub, try it in a side project, and see if it fits your workflow.
